title: Sr Program Specialist - Construction, Fire or BAS Background
description:
As a Sr. Construction Manager, you will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of multi-year, multisite national programs, managing teams to ensure project schedules, design, execution, testing, closeout, and turnover to service are delivered with consistent quality and speed to satisfy contractual requirements. You will develop mechanisms for monitoring project progress and provide intervention and problem-solving support in partnership with the FAA Sr. Program Manager, project managers, and customers.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Grow the business, manage change, and ensure all contractual obligations are met.
  • Manage multiple projects simultaneously in a lean administrative environment, demonstrating initiative and accountability. Lead and influence cross-functional teams to ensure contractual deliverables are completed within established timelines.
  • Coordinate, plan, schedule, and monitor project implementation, including project schedules, budgets, and financial performance.
  • Manage subcontractor procurement, scheduling, coordination, and performance to ensure project requirements are met.
  • Apply knowledge of construction dispute resolution processes, contract documents, labor laws, construction contracts, and construction administration to minimize project risk.
  • Anticipate, identify, evaluate, and negotiate changes to the documented scope of work.
  • Monitor project progress, identify potential issues, and implement corrective actions to maintain schedules, budgets, and quality standards.
  • Partner with the FAA Sr. Program Manager, project managers, and customers to resolve project challenges and support successful program execution.
  • Maintain professional, effective communication with internal stakeholders, customers, subcontractors, and other project partners.
  • Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with company policies, reporting requirements, and contractual commitments.
  • Oversee project testing, closeout, and turnover to service to ensure consistent quality and successful completion.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • 5 or more years of experience in Architecture-Engineering and Design/Build programs.
  • 5 or more years of competitive construction industry experience managing programs or projects exceeding $4 million.
  • 3 or more years of Fire Alarm experience.
  • Familiarity with NFPA 72, NFPA 101, and fire alarm systems.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to contractual and export control requirements.
  • Ability to complete and pass an FAA background check.

WE VALUE

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Project Management Institute (PMI) certification.
  • Certification or experience with XLS140 and XLS3000 Fire Detection, Suppression, and Mass Notification Control Systems.
  • Xtralis VESDA accreditation.
  • NICET Level III or higher certification.
  • Experience managing complex, multisite construction programs and coordinating cross-functional teams.
  • Strong project planning, scheduling, budgeting, risk management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, stakeholder management, and subcontractor oversight skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to changing project requirements, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

Candidates must be able to complete and pass an FAA background check.

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and the opportunity to develop solutions alongside dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. Benefits include employer-subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match; Flexible Spending Accounts; Health Savings Accounts; Employee Assistance Program (EAP); Educational Assistance; Parental Leave; Paid Time Off for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave; and 12 paid holidays. Learn more about Honeywell benefits

ABOUT HONEYWELL TECHNOLOGIES

Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovation focused on solving the world's most mission-critical challenges and enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial, and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions, and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector's transition from automation to autonomy. title: (CAN) Pharmacy Assistant
description:
Position Summary...

The Pharmacy Assistant assists the Pharmacist in the technical aspects of prescription filling and administrative duties in order to increase the Pharmacist's opportunity to provide patient care. The Pharmacy Assistant is expected to participate in all aspects of Pharmacy Operations required of a team player. They are a key member in the delivery of superior customer service.

What you'll do...

1. Receiving prescriptions from patients, following provincial legal/regulatory conditions and assessing the prescription for completeness i.e. Name; Address; DOB; Allergies; 3rd Party Information; Any Special Requests; Prescriber; Generic/Brand; Prioritizing Prescriptions with 21st Century Guidelines.
2. Performing Computer Functions as directed by the Pharmacist i.e. Data Entry; Price Check; Patient Information Entry/Update; Competent interpretation and processing of written prescriptions including Latin abbreviations, drug name recognition, dosage calculations; Refills; Report Generation; Patient Profile checks.
3. title: Stockperson/Cartpusher
description:
Position Summary...

As a Stockperson / Cartpusher, you play an important role in creating a safe, organized, and welcoming shopping experience for customers. You are responsible for collecting shopping carts from cart corrals, the parking lot, and the store perimeter and returning them to designated storage locations using approved procedures. Through friendly customer interactions and a strong focus on safety, this role supports smooth store operations while building valuable skills in retail, teamwork, and customer service.

What you'll do...

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Support Customer Service Operations
Collect shopping carts from cart corrals, the parking lot, and store perimeter, and return them safely to designated storage areas using Walmart approved procedures. Ensure required logs are completed accurately.

Respond to Customer and Store Needs
Respond promptly to requests from all registers and Customer Service, including assisting customers with carry outs and carry ins and verifying receipts for proof of purchase when required.

Maintain Clean Facilities and Equipment
Perform occasional cleaning and maintenance duties, including restrooms, while following established guidelines for chemical handling, proper disposal procedures, and safe use of power equipment. Complete required equipment inspections before use.

Follow Safety Standards and Procedures
Adhere to all safety and emergency protocols, including hazardous communication, lockout/tagout, and bloodborne pathogen guidelines, to maintain a safe environment for customers and associates.

Promote a Safe and Hazard Free Work Environment
Use required personal protective equipment, including steel toe footwear and a reflective vest, complete safety sweeps as required, and follow Company policies and procedures to support a clean, safe workplace.

title: (CAN) Pharmacy Assistant
description:
Position Summary...

The Pharmacy Assistant assists the Pharmacist in the technical aspects of prescription filling and administrative duties in order to increase the Pharmacist's opportunity to provide patient care. The Pharmacy Assistant is expected to participate in all aspects of Pharmacy Operations required of a team player. They are a key member in the delivery of superior customer service.

What you'll do...

1. Receiving prescriptions from patients, following provincial legal/regulatory conditions and assessing the prescription for completeness i.e. Name; Address; DOB; Allergies; 3rd Party Information; Any Special Requests; Prescriber; Generic/Brand; Prioritizing Prescriptions with 21st Century Guidelines.
2. Performing Computer Functions as directed by the Pharmacist i.e. Data Entry; Price Check; Patient Information Entry/Update; Competent interpretation and processing of written prescriptions including Latin abbreviations, drug name recognition, dosage calculations; Refills; Report Generation; Patient Profile checks.
3. Filling prescriptions (always under the Pharmacist’s supervision), selecting appropriate products, performing the accuracy program, including 7 point, Visual and DIN checks, selecting and counting/ measuring & preparing appropriate products, labeling and organizing for pharmacist checking, gaining necessary approvals for verbal refills where authorized, employing 'STOP' forms if applicable and facilitating all aspects of Cognitive Services.
4. Maintaining Inventory Control, assisting Pharmacist in maintaining appropriate stock levels of drugs and supplies, checking for and pulling expired medications at least monthly, cleaning up Will Call Bin of 'stale' prescriptions on a regular basis, writing up returns, ordering of drugs and supplies, using preferred wholesaler for Pharmacy purchases as much as possible i.e. Kohl and Frisch, operating of the Telxon gun, checking off, pricing and putting away pharmacy orders, zoning the pharmacy shelves, 'X- ing' bottles when opened and interchangeable drug knowledge and appropriate maintenance/selection of key brands/preferred generics.
5. General Housekeeping, stocking Prescription filling supplies (Vials, labels, bags), keeping the dispensary clean, organized and neat, maintaining clean/safe work environment as part of the team approach (i.e. dishes, garbage) and maintaining & cleaning packaging & dispensing equipment, computer, fax machine, etc.
6. Clerical Organization, filing prescriptions, invoices, reports, correspondence and memos and completing any administrative support functions assigned (i.e. journals, accounts receivable, Aged Trial Balance).
7. Assisting with OTC Operations and ordering, stocking, cashier duties as assigned by OTC Manager and/or Pharmacist.

The pay range for this position is $20.15 - $26.42/hr. Rate of pay will be determined based on relevant experience.

R-2664217

title: Content Lead - The Longevity Show
location: London, England and Wales, United Kingdom
description:
We are looking for a Content Lead to shape what our audiences hear and learn at our Longevity Show events, so that every attendee leaves inspired and with tangible takeaways.

Our inaugural edition at Tobacco Dock in June 2026 drew 3000+ attendees, 160+ speakers, 100+ partner and exhibitors with a sold out expo and 200+ to a gala dinner. 87% of our partners and exhibitors rated the experience as very good or excellent and 7!% said they would come back in 2027 - proof the proposition works.

We are now scaling fast. London returns to tobacco Dock on 16-17 April 2027 for a bigger, more ambitious second edition, alongside plans to launch The Longevity show in New York - building the platform for the world's most active longevity market. This is your chance to shape the narrative, content and experience our audience have, and build this franchise globally

The Longevity Show brings together the public, practitioners, founders, investors and scientists around one question: how do we live longer, healthier lives? Our content sits at the heart of that, from main-stage keynotes for a consumer audience to senior-level conversations at our B2B conference.

You will own the overall content programme, and our audiences experience will be at the heart of your decision making. This is a senior, hands-on role in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial business. As our events portfolio grows, there is real scope for the role, and the person in it, to grow with it.

Core focus areas

The role currently centres on two programmes. Our events evolve every year, and the focus will evolve with them.

  1. The Longevity Show content programme. Our consumer show programme: accessible, inspiring and practical sessions that help the public understand longevity and act on it.
  2. The B2B conference content programme. A senior-level agenda that blends science, innovation, investment and industry trends, positioning the conference as the leading platform for the longevity sector.

Key responsibilities

Content strategy and curation

  • Set and deliver the content vision for The Longevity Show and the B2B conference.
  • Build compelling agendas that blend science, innovation, consumer trends and investment insight.
  • Structure each programme so it flows across keynotes, firesides, panels, workshops live demos and experiential content.
  • Turn complex scientific and technical topics into formats that land with each audience.
  • Work with our co-founder, and in-house longevity subject matter expert, and our wider network of advisors (curated by you) to keep programming at the cutting edge.

Speaker acquisition and management

  • Identify and secure high-profile speakers, and content creators thought leaders and innovators from health, biotech, wellness and longevity.
  • Build and manage speaker and content led relationships, ensuring world-class delivery on stage.
  • Manage the speaker pipeline, briefings and session preparation from first approach to show day.

Audience and thought leadership

  • Make sure every session gives attendees clear, practical takeaways.
  • Position our events as the leading longevity platform by curating conversations that move the industry forward.
  • Track emerging research, trends and technologies to keep the programme fresh and future-facing.
  • Support year-round content (articles, video, digital programming) that builds momentum before and after each event.
  • Gather audience feedback and use it to improve the programme year on year.

Commercial and sponsor integration

  • Partner with the sponsorship team to align content with sponsor objectives while safeguarding content integrity.
  • Integrate sponsor and partner expertise into the programme authentically.
  • Contribute content ideas to sponsorship packages to maximise partner impact.

Cross-team collaboration

  • Work with the Event Director on overall programme strategy.
  • Partner with marketing to turn content into audience acquisition campaigns and support the ticket sales strategy.
  • Partner with the Experience Lead so the content programme and the wider show feel joined up for attendees, offering:
    • insight from the programme, speakers and audience feedback to shape on-site experiences;
    • introductions and relationships from your speaker and partner network;
    • support in identifying memorable experiences that bring the content to life.
  • Coordinate with operations and production teams to deliver flawless on-stage execution.

Requirements

  • 4+ years of content or programme curation experience in conferences, summits, festivals or thought-leadership events.
  • A track record of building agendas and securing senior-level speakers.
  • A strong content instinct, able to turn complex scientific and technical topics into engaging formats for both consumer and professional audiences.
  • An excellent network across health, wellness, biotech and consumer longevity, or a demonstrable ability to build one quickly.
  • A skilled relationship builder, comfortable working with sponsors and partners while protecting editorial quality.
  • Naturally curious about health, wellness and innovation.
  • Creative, detail-oriented and highly organised, able to manage many stakeholders and deadlines at once.
  • Ambitious, keen to grow with the business, and comfortable in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

Benefits

We offer a range of flexible, discretionary benefits to our team. These currently include:

  • 25 days contractual annual leave
  • Enhanced discretionary leave provision, including an additional day off for your birthday and leave between Christmas and New Year's Day
  • The option to work remotely anywhere in the world for 3 weeks/year (1 week at Easter and 2 weeks during July and August)
  • Private healthcare package
  • Mental health, wellbeing, and learning and development stipends
  • Lunch 1x/week, office snacks, and regular team drinks
  • Quarterly team activities and annual team trip/day out
  • Access to the Founders Forum Group network of businesses and wider tech ecosystem

We currently have a hybrid working model with 4 days spent in the office and 1 day with the option to work remotely/from home.

title: Welding Engineer
description:
MATRIX is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Welding Engineer to join our dynamic team. In this position, the Welding Engineer will support a large project at McGuire Nuclear Station. This individual will be responsible for managing the weld program and providing technical support for construction activities. The role requires close coordination with work planners, Quality Assurance/Quality Control, engineering, project management, and field craft to ensure welding activities meet applicable project requirements, codes, and specifications.

DURATION: 12 months with potential for extension
WORK SCHEDULE: This is a 5 8-hour day schedule – This will increase during outage periods
PER DIEM: Yes
LOCATION: Onsite in Jackson, SC for 2-week training. The project assignment will be onsite at McGuire Nuclear in Huntersville, NC.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBLITIES:
  • Manage implementation and maintenance of the weld program for the assigned project scope.
  • Develop and maintain weld maps, weld tracking logs, and supporting fabrication documentation.
  • Review welding procedure specifications, procedure qualification records, and welder qualifications for applicability to planned work.
  • Provide technical guidance on welding processes, material selection, filler metals, preheat, and post-weld heat treatment requirements, as applicable.
  • Coordinate with fabrication and quality teams on weld sequencing, inspection requirements, traceability, and documentation.
  • Support resolution of welding issues, nonconformances, and weld repairs.
  • Monitor fabrication activities for compliance with approved procedures and project requirements.
  • Support compilation and review of completed weld records and turnover documentation.
  • Perform primarily office and non-manual work.
  • Perform work related to the management or general business operations of MATRIX or its customers/clients, while exercising discretion and independent judgment with respect to matters of significance to MATRIX and its customers/clients.
  • Interface with managers or head of a unit/department requiring the integration of multiple functional organizations.
  • Use “lessons learned” to improve quality of MATRIX’s future projects; make recommendations to MATRIX as to the implementations of future policies and procedures.

QUALIFICATIONS:

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
  • Relevant engineering degree or equivalent combination of technical education and welding engineering experience.
  • Experience supporting weld engineering and fabrication activities in nuclear or other highly regulated industrial environments.
  • Ability to manage a project weld program, including welding procedures, welder qualifications, weld traceability, and supporting records.
  • Experience developing and maintaining weld maps, weld logs, and fabrication documentation.
  • Working knowledge of applicable welding codes, standards, and project specifications.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, welding symbols, and welding procedure specifications.
  • Experience coordinating with fabrication supervision, engineering, and QA/QC to resolve welding and inspection issues.
  • Strong communication, organization, and documentation skills.
  • Must meet applicable client and site access, screening, training, and badging requirements.
  • Available to support the project work schedule, including overtime or shift work as required.
  • Able to work in an active fabrication and construction environment and comply with site safety and PPE requirements.
  • The ability to communicate well both verbally and written as a business necessity to ensure the safe and efficient operations of business. Clear, concise, and effective fluency in the English language is essential.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
  • Prior experience supporting nuclear power plant construction, modifications, or major fabrication projects.
  • Previous experience working with client welding programs and procedures.
  • Familiarity with ASME Section IX and applicable ASME construction codes.
  • Experience supporting weld repairs, nonconformance resolution, and final documentation turnover.
  • Familiarity with nondestructive examination methods and inspection coordination.
  • AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification or equivalent welding inspection credentials.

Partner with merchandising, legal, finance, supply chain, packaging, and IT teams to ensure accurate data capture and timely reporting.


Develop and maintain internal controls, SOPs, and governance routines that support auditability and reduce compliance risk.


Manage relationships with Producer Responsibility Organizations (PROs), regulators, industry associations, and external advisors.


Monitor legislative changes and assess business impact, including proactive recommendations for risk mitigation and process changes.


Drive continuous improvement initiatives to optimize program costs and improve reporting efficiency.


Prepare executive updates that summarize compliance status, financial exposure, upcoming regulatory changes, and strategic recommendations.


Manage a team of associates in the applicable areas


Qualifications:


Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Sustainability, Engineering, Public Policy, Business, or related discipline (Master's degree preferred).


6 to 8 years of relevant experience in environmental compliance, producer responsibility, sustainability operations, or regulatory programs.


Demonstrated experience managing Canadian EPR and/or eco-fee compliance programs.


Strong understanding of provincial stewardship frameworks, Blue Box obligations, and eco-fee methodologies.


Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives in a complex, matrixed organization.


Strong analytical and financial acumen with the ability to validate data and interpret fee impacts.


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level reporting.


High attention to detail and strong project management capabilities.

Preferred Experience


Experience working with retailers, consumer goods, packaging-intensive industries, or producer organizations.


Exposure to environmental data systems, reporting automation, and dashboarding tools.


Experience supporting internal and external compliance audits.

Receiving and Unloading Merchandise
Prepares and resets the Receiving Area and unloads general merchandise trailers, including completing live unloading of remaining merchandise.

Handle and Move Merchandise Safely
Maintains cold chain standards for refrigerated and frozen products and pulls pallets of merchandise to the sales floor for overnight processing.

Stocking and Customer Support
Assists with stocking the sales floor as assigned and provides customer service when needed to support a positive shopping experience.

Overstock Organization
Labels and places overstock merchandise in designated areas to support efficient inventory management.

• Performs repetitive tasks such as stocking, zoning, and organizing products with attention to detail and consistency to uphold store standards.

R-2658823

title: Associate Graphic Designer
description:
Position Summary...

The Associate Graphic Designer supports the development of original, commercially relevant graphic artwork for apparel across Kids and Adult categories. Working within the Apparel Product Development team, this role creates seasonal graphics, prints and graphic components that align to customer needs, brand direction, trend research and product-development timelines. The role collaborates with a broad range of cross-functional partners to deliver creative, production-ready artwork that meets quality, cost and supplier requirements.

What you'll do...

The Associate Graphic Designer manages the development and ongoing maintenance of digital content catalogues and stock libraries. This role partners with key stakeholders across the organization to design visual content that aids in communication and storytelling. The position may also involve collaborating with video production teams to create supporting assets.

The Associate Graphic Designer supports the creation of seasonal graphics for various product categories, including apparel and home. This involves building graphic components that meet production limitations and standards, as well as creating illustrations and graphics in various styles appropriate for different customer segments using tools like Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop.

Effective time management and organizational skills are essential, as the role requires juggling multiple projects across divisions and meeting tight deadlines. The designer must handle constructive criticism from multiple stakeholders and adjust artwork and style as needed. The position may also require managing third-party design resources and ensuring consistency in style guides and brand standards.

The Associate Graphic Designer identifies opportunities for innovation within branding standards and works to improve both associate and customer experiences related to storytelling and tone. This role formats and prepares seasonal palettes for technical use and coordinates with various teams to achieve development goals and maintain permanent files.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Post-secondary education in Graphic Design, Fashion Design or a related field.
  • Experience creating original graphics for apparel, fashion or a consumer-product environment is preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, particularly Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop, with a strong understanding of file setup and artwork preparation for apparel production.
  • Strong skills in illustration, typography, print and pattern development, with the ability to create graphics for varied customer segments and product categories.
  • Knowledge of apparel graphic production requirements, including supplier-ready artwork, colour callouts, placement, scale and production limitations.
  • Strong awareness of fashion, graphic, print and cultural trends, with the ability to translate trend direction into commercially relevant product graphics.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines while collaborating effectively with Design, Product Development, Merchandising, Sourcing and other cross-functional partners.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating original graphic design work, creative versatility and an understanding of apparel graphics.

Leadership Expectations:

Respect the Individual:

Demonstrates and encourages respect for others; drives a positive associate and customer experience for all; embraces differences in people, cultures, ideas, and experiences; supports workplaces where associated feel seen and connected through a culture of belonging, so all associates thrive and perform; contributes to an environment allowing everyone to bring their best selves to work.

Demonstrates engagement and commitment to the team, developing others through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and developmental opportunities; and recognizes others’ contributions and accomplishments.

Builds strong and trusting relationships with team members and business partners; works collaboratively to achieve objectives; communicates with impact and listens attentively to a range of audiences; and demonstrates energy and positivity for own work.

Acts with Integrity:

Maintains and promotes the highest standards of integrity, ethics and compliance; models the Walmart values and leads by example to foster our culture; supports Walmart’s goal of becoming a regenerative company by making a positive impact for associates, customers, and the world around us (e.g., creating a sense of belonging, eliminating waste, participating in local giving).

Follows the law, our code of conduct and company policies, and encourages others to do the same; supports an environment where associates feel comfortable sharing concerns; reinforces our culture of non-retaliation; listens to concerns raised by associates and takes action; acts with accountability for achieving results in a way that is consistent with our values.

Is consistently humble, self-aware, honest, and transparent.

Serve our Customers:

Delivers results while putting the customer first and applying an omni-merchant mindset and acts with an Every Day Low Cost mindset to drive value and Every Day Low Prices for customers.

Adopts a broad perspective that considers data, analytics, customer insights, and different parts of the business when making plans.

Strive for Excellence:

Consistently raises the bar and seeks to improve; demonstrates curiosity and a growth mindset; seeks feedback, asks thoughtful questions; supports innovation and intelligent risk-taking; and exhibits resilience in the face of setbacks.

Implements and supports continuous improvements and willingly embraces new digital tools and ways of working.

The pay range for this position is $74,000.00 - $101,750.00. Pay will be determined based on relevant experience.

title: (CAN) Meat Associate
description:
Position Summary...

Working as a Meat Associate at Walmart Canada is a great opportunity to grow your skills in a fast‑paced retail environment. In this role, you deliver outstanding customer service by living Walmart’s values, keeping the meat department clean, organized, and well‑stocked, and supporting daily sales activities. As part of the team, you help create a fresh, inviting shopping experience for customers. This role is ideal for individuals who enjoy hands‑on work, teamwork, and making a positive impact on every customer visit.

What you'll do...

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Maintain Department Organization and Standards
Keeps the department clean, organized, and properly zoned to ensure it is customer-ready at all times. Rotates stock regularly and removes expired or unsellable products.

Ensure Accurate Pricing and Signing
Ensures all merchandise is correctly signed and priced. Follows established procedures for ordering, clearance, markups and markdowns, signing, flagging, pricing, and labeling.

Follow Food Safety and Cold Chain Practices
Adheres to food safety and cold chain standards, including temperature checks, thermometer calibration, proper food handling, product rotation, sell-by dates, and expiration date compliance.

Prepare and Serve Deli Products
Takes customer orders and prepares deli items such as meat, cheese, and fried chicken. Uses slicers, stackers, rotisserie ovens, deep fryers, and other tools safely to prepare food, fill display cases, and complete special customer orders.

Health and Safety Compliance
Follows all Health and Safety guidelines and Company policies to maintain a safe, clean, and hygienic work environment.

Flexibility (Availability/Work Schedule)
• Be open to working a variety of shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, based on business needs. Your adaptability helps ensure the store runs smoothly and customers receive consistent, high-quality service.

POTENTIAL CHALLENGES IN THIS ROLE

High Task Volume in a Fast-Paced Environment
• Manages overnight hours effectively and planning accordingly to stay energized and focused.
• Effectively manages work hours and plans ahead to maintain energy and focus throughout the shift.
• Handles a fast-paced workload with efficiency, ensuring large volumes of restocking and recovery are completed accurately and on time.

Physical Demands
• Performs physical tasks such as standing for extended periods, bending, and lifting inventory, equipment, or supplies weighing up to 20 lbs., and occasionally up to 50 lbs.
• Performs repetitive tasks such as stocking, zoning, and organizing products with attention to detail and consistency to uphold store standards.

WHY YOU'LL ENJOY WORKING HERE

Energetic, Fast-Paced Environment
Thrive in a dynamic setting where every day brings something new.

Appreciation for Your Efforts
Your contributions are recognized and valued.

Career Growth Opportunities
Build your skills and advance your career with us.

Meaningful Impact
Take pride in helping customers save money and live better.

title: Coding Quality Analyst
description:
Work Schedule:
1.0 FTE, 40 hours per week. Scheduled shifts will be discussed in the interview process. Hours may vary based on the operational needs of the department.

This is a remote position. To be eligible to work remotely, you must be in an approved remote work state for UW Health. We’ve included a link below to view the full list of approved remote work states.


Approved Remote Work States Listing

Be part of something remarkable

Join the #1 hospital in Wisconsin!

We are seeking a Coding Quality Analyst to:

  • Develop and implement an organized monitoring system for the QA program structure.
  • Develop, conduct, and/or coordinate the review process for coding quality. This includes, analyzing errors and formulating advice/education, identifying and advising staff on quality improvement opportunities, participating in individualized feedback for coding staff, and summarizing results and identifying trends for specific educational opportunities.
  • Prepare summary reporting of the coding review results as requested.


At UW Health, you will have:

  • An excellent benefits package, including health and dental insurance, paid time off and retirement plans.
  • Options for a variety of schedules and shifts that offer flexibility and allow for work-life balance.
  • Access to UW Health’s Wellness Options at Work that support employee/family well-being.
  • Tuition reimbursement eligibility after 1 year of employment - UW Health invests in your professional growth by helping pay for coursework associated with career advancement.

Qualifications

  • Medical Coding Program Graduate required.
  • Graduate of a Health Information Technology program preferred.

Work Experience

  • Non-HCC roles: Experience with coding concepts (Current Procedural Terminology (CPT), International Classification of Disease 10th Edition-Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM), and Health Care Procedure Coding System (HCPCS)
  • 3 years progressive coding experience (for non-HCC roles) or 3 years of experience in HCC Risk Adjustment (for HCC roles) required
  • 3 years progressive coding experience in multiple specialties (non-HCC roles) or 3 years HCC Risk Adjustment Coding at a large health system or academic medical center (for HCC roles) preferred

Licenses & Certifications

  • For Non-HCC roles: Certification as Certified Professional Coder (CPC), Certified Outpatient Coder (COC), Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC), Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), or Certified Coding Specialist Physician-Based (CCS-P) Upon Hire Required
  • For HCC-specific roles: Certified Risk Adjustment Coder (CRC) within 1 Year Required
  • Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT) or Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA) Preferred

title: Senior Communications Specialist (Internal Communications)
description:
Align yourself with an organization that has a reputation for excellence! Cedars-Sinai was awarded the National Research Corporation’s Consumer Choice Award 19 years in a row for providing the highest-quality medical care in Los Angeles. We also were awarded the Advisory Board Company’s Workplace of the Year. This annual award recognizes hospitals and health systems nationwide that have high levels of employee engagement. We provide an outstanding benefit package that includes healthcare, paid time off, and a 403(b). Join us! Discover why U.S. News & World Report has named us one of America’s Best Hospitals.

What are you responsible for?

The Senior Communications Specialist will develop and implement strategic communications plans and activities to promote and support Cedars-Sinai’s employee-facing initiatives. This individual will play a key role in identifying strategic, innovative news, feature and communications ideas for various communications channels; write and develop stories, collateral materials and other content; edit written materials; work with the visuals team to manage and assign photos; and assist in the production of internal publications and updates. Must demonstrate exceptional, accurate writing ability and highly effective, courteous, professional and respectful communication skills in daily interactions with physicians, nurses, staff members and others. Must be able to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast paced, high-volume environment with frequent interruptions.

Collaborates and works cross-functionally with internal collaborators in Marketing and Communications as well as with external partners throughout Cedars-Sinai. Handles basic design and implementation of communication materials through specialized templates. Works collaboratively with other members of the Organizational Communications team to manage priorities, workflows and shared responsibilities and assignments. Primary duties include:

Responsible for leading and/or supporting essential communications, projects, and initiatives to further Cedars-Sinai’s organizational priorities as well as external and internal communications goals.

Strategizes, writes, edits and publishes content for Cedars-Sinai staff, medical staff and patients, including but not limited to news and feature stories, FAQs and talking points, memos and announcements, collateral copy, blog posts, collateral content website copy. Ensures all copy and content are clear, well-written, grammatically correct and factually accurate.

Covers clinical-departmental beats as assigned to support the Organizational Communications team.

Contributes to crisis response, serving as an agile and flexible writer and working on-call as needed.

Works in various digital platforms, including email campaign, intranet and digital channel platforms supporting content creation and distribution.

Collaborates closely with External Communications, Social Media, Creative Services, Brand Strategy and other Marketing and Communications teams to promote high-value stories and communications, in support of departmental and organizational strategic priorities.

Establishes and maintains effective relationships and processes with all internal cross-functional collaborators to effectively execute on collaboration needs. Interacts with physicians, research investigators, operations staff, patients and others in a professional and responsive manner, protecting patient privacy in all facets of work.

Delivers cleanly written, accurate stories and communications to support staff, medical staff, programs and other aspects of Cedars-Sinai. Adheres to deadlines and internal style guides.

Serves as an all-purpose collaborator, supporting Organizational Communications team members across functions and beats with writing and strategy support as needed.

Please provide two or more writing samples illustrating internal communications, along with your resume, when applying for this role.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in English, journalism, communications or a related field required.
  • A minimum of 5 years of experience writing, editing, developing and delivering in-depth content or related communications experience required. A minimum of 7 or more years of experience writing, editing, developing and delivering in-depth content or related communications experience preferred.
  • Proven experience of at least 5 years in an academic medical center, hospital or healthcare, broadcast news, nonprofit and/or foundation experience strongly preferred.

Why work here?

Beyond outstanding employee benefits including paid vacation plus 10 paid holidays, a 403(b) and our Choice Retirement plan (100% funded by Cedars-Sinai) we take pride in hiring the best employees. Our accomplished staff reflects the culturally and ethnically diverse community we serve. They are proof of our commitment to creating a dynamic, inclusive environment that fuels innovation.

title: (CAN) Pharmacy Assistant
description:
Position Summary...

The Pharmacy Assistant assists the Pharmacist in the technical aspects of prescription filling and administrative duties in order to increase the Pharmacist's opportunity to provide patient care. The Pharmacy Assistant is expected to participate in all aspects of Pharmacy Operations required of a team player. They are a key member in the delivery of superior customer service.

What you'll do...

1. Receiving prescriptions from patients, following provincial legal/regulatory conditions and assessing the prescription for completeness i.e. Name; Address; DOB; Allergies; 3rd Party Information; Any Special Requests; Prescriber; Generic/Brand; Prioritizing Prescriptions with 21st Century Guidelines.
2. Performing Computer Functions as directed by the Pharmacist i.e. Data Entry; Price Check; Patient Information Entry/Update; Competent interpretation and processing of written prescriptions including Latin abbreviations, drug name recognition, dosage calculations; Refills; Report Generation; Patient Profile checks.
3. Filling prescriptions (always under the Pharmacist’s supervision), selecting appropriate products, performing the accuracy program, including 7 point, Visual and DIN checks, selecting and counting/ measuring & preparing appropriate products, labeling and organizing for pharmacist checking, gaining necessary approvals for verbal refills where authorized, employing 'STOP' forms if applicable and facilitating all aspects of Cognitive Services.
4. Maintaining Inventory Control, assisting Pharmacist in maintaining appropriate stock levels of drugs and supplies, checking for and pulling expired medications at least monthly, cleaning up Will Call Bin of 'stale' prescriptions on a regular basis, writing up returns, ordering of drugs and supplies, using preferred wholesaler for Pharmacy purchases as much as possible i.e. Kohl and Frisch, operating of the Telxon gun, checking off, pricing and putting away pharmacy orders, zoning the pharmacy shelves, 'X- ing' bottles when opened and interchangeable drug knowledge and appropriate maintenance/selection of key brands/preferred generics.
5. General Housekeeping, stocking Prescription filling supplies (Vials, labels, bags), keeping the dispensary clean, organized and neat, maintaining clean/safe work environment as part of the team approach (i.e. dishes, garbage) and maintaining & cleaning packaging & dispensing equipment, computer, fax machine, etc.
6. Clerical Organization, filing prescriptions, invoices, reports, correspondence and memos and completing any administrative support functions assigned (i.e. journals, accounts receivable, Aged Trial Balance).
7. Assisting with OTC Operations and ordering, stocking, cashier duties as assigned by OTC Manager and/or Pharmacist.

The pay range for this position is $17.60 - $23.10/hr. Rate of pay will be determined based on relevant experience.

title: (CAN) Pharmacy Assistant
description:
Position Summary...

The Pharmacy Assistant assists the Pharmacist in the technical aspects of prescription filling and administrative duties in order to increase the Pharmacist's opportunity to provide patient care. The Pharmacy Assistant is expected to participate in all aspects of Pharmacy Operations required of a team player. They are a key member in the delivery of superior customer service.

What you'll do...

1. Receiving prescriptions from patients, following provincial legal/regulatory conditions and assessing the prescription for completeness i.e. Name; Address; DOB; Allergies; 3rd Party Information; Any Special Requests; Prescriber; Generic/Brand; Prioritizing Prescriptions with 21st Century Guidelines.
2. Performing Computer Functions as directed by the Pharmacist i.e. Data Entry; Price Check; Patient Information Entry/Update; Competent interpretation and processing of written prescriptions including Latin abbreviations, drug name recognition, dosage calculations; Refills; Report Generation; Patient Profile checks.
3. Filling prescriptions (always under the Pharmacist’s supervision), selecting appropriate products, performing the accuracy program, including 7 point, Visual and DIN checks, selecting and counting/ measuring & preparing appropriate products, labeling and organizing for pharmacist checking, gaining necessary approvals for verbal refills where authorized, employing 'STOP' forms if applicable and facilitating all aspects of Cognitive Services.
4. Maintaining Inventory Control, assisting Pharmacist in maintaining appropriate stock levels of drugs and supplies, checking for and pulling expired medications at least monthly, cleaning up Will Call Bin of 'stale' prescriptions on a regular basis, writing up returns, ordering of drugs and supplies, using preferred wholesaler for Pharmacy purchases as much as possible i.e. Kohl and Frisch, operating of the Telxon gun, checking off, pricing and putting away pharmacy orders, zoning the pharmacy shelves, 'X- ing' bottles when opened and interchangeable drug knowledge and appropriate maintenance/selection of key brands/preferred generics.
5. General Housekeeping, stocking Prescription filling supplies (Vials, labels, bags), keeping the dispensary clean, organized and neat, maintaining clean/safe work environment as part of the team approach (i.e. dishes, garbage) and maintaining & cleaning packaging & dispensing equipment, computer, fax machine, etc.
6. Clerical Organization, filing prescriptions, invoices, reports, correspondence and memos and completing any administrative support functions assigned (i.e. journals, accounts receivable, Aged Trial Balance).
7. Assisting with OTC Operations and ordering, stocking, cashier duties as assigned by OTC Manager and/or Pharmacist.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
MATRIX is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Project Manager to join our dynamic team. In this position, we are looking for strong mechanical and piping background.

DURATION: Approximately 18 months
WORK SCHEDULE: Approximately 18 months
PER DIEM: Yes

LOCATION: Port Gibson, MS

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBLITIES:
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of projects as assigned and within the parameters of cost, quality, schedule and objectives.
• Oversee all aspects of projects.
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize progress of project.
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding the status of projects.
• Provide leadership for project team members and the Project Management process; lead and direct the work of others, with primary duties to customarily and regularly direct the work of two or more other employees, including but not limited to more junior staff in employee’s discipline; make substantive recommendations to Matrix as to the hiring, firing or discipline of employees.
• Follow and adhere to Project Management Process and Requirements.
• Maintain “Stop Work” authority as to the project.
• Use independent discretion to declare Stop Work if any unsafe situation arises that puts personnel, the project or equipment in jeopardy.
• Educate MATRIX and client on project goals, operations and safety.
• Ensure compliance with health, safety, and environmental regulations and guidelines; promote health and safety awareness consciousness and implements all MATRIX health and safety procedures.
• Perform primarily office and non-manual work.
• Perform work related to the management or general business operations of MATRIX or its customers/clients, while exercising discretion and independent judgment with respect to matters of significance to MATRIX and its customers/clients.
• Interface with managers or head of a unit/department requiring the integration of multiple functional organizations.
• Use “lessons learned” to improve quality of MATRIX’s future projects; make recommendations to MATRIX as to the implementations of future policies and procedures.

QUALIFICATIONS:

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• 15+ years of experience in power plant operations or equivalent military experience.
• Minimum of 10 years project management experience required.
• Nuclear experience is required.
• PMP certification desired.
• The ability to communicate well both verbally and written as a business necessity to ensure the safe and efficient operations of business. Clear, concise and effective fluency in the English language is essential.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• The employee is self-motivated and has a willingness to learn.
• Has extensive knowledge of nuclear applications.
• Familiar with a variety of the field’s concepts, practices, and procedures.
• A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected.
• Able to handle high paced work environment.
• The ability to communicate well with customers and other Matrix and customer/client employees.
• Must be dependable.
• Must have proficient computer skills.

title: (CAN) Pharmacy Assistant
description:
Position Summary...

The Pharmacy Assistant assists the Pharmacist in the technical aspects of prescription filling and administrative duties in order to increase the Pharmacist's opportunity to provide patient care. The Pharmacy Assistant is expected to participate in all aspects of Pharmacy Operations required of a team player. They are a key member in the delivery of superior customer service.

What you'll do...

1. Receiving prescriptions from patients, following provincial legal/regulatory conditions and assessing the prescription for completeness i.e. Name; Address; DOB; Allergies; 3rd Party Information; Any Special Requests; Prescriber; Generic/Brand; Prioritizing Prescriptions with 21st Century Guidelines.
2. Performing Computer Functions as directed by the Pharmacist i.e. Data Entry; Price Check; Patient Information Entry/Update; Competent interpretation and processing of written prescriptions including Latin abbreviations, drug name recognition, dosage calculations; Refills; Report Generation; Patient Profile checks.
3. Filling prescriptions (always under the Pharmacist’s supervision), selecting appropriate products, performing the accuracy program, including 7 point, Visual and DIN checks, selecting and counting/ measuring & preparing appropriate products, labeling and organizing for pharmacist checking, gaining necessary approvals for verbal refills where authorized, employing 'STOP' forms if applicable and facilitating all aspects of Cognitive Services.
4. Maintaining Inventory Control, assisting Pharmacist in maintaining appropriate stock levels of drugs and supplies, checking for and pulling expired medications at least monthly, cleaning up Will Call Bin of 'stale' prescriptions on a regular basis, writing up returns, ordering of drugs and supplies, using preferred wholesaler for Pharmacy purchases as much as possible i.e. Kohl and Frisch, operating of the Telxon gun, checking off, pricing and putting away pharmacy orders, zoning the pharmacy shelves, 'X- ing' bottles when opened and interchangeable drug knowledge and appropriate maintenance/selection of key brands/preferred generics.
5. General Housekeeping, stocking Prescription filling supplies (Vials, labels, bags), keeping the dispensary clean, organized and neat, maintaining clean/safe work environment as part of the team approach (i.e. dishes, garbage) and maintaining & cleaning packaging & dispensing equipment, computer, fax machine, etc.
6. Clerical Organization, filing prescriptions, invoices, reports, correspondence and memos and completing any administrative support functions assigned (i.e. journals, accounts receivable, Aged Trial Balance).
7. Assisting with OTC Operations and ordering, stocking, cashier duties as assigned by OTC Manager and/or Pharmacist.

The pay range for this position is $17.60 - $23.10/hr. Rate of pay will be determined based on relevant experience.

title: Senior Manager, Process Improvement
description:
Position Summary...

The Senior Manager, Process Improvement is responsible for leading strategic development and execution of process improvement and innovation projects to support business objectives. This role ensures alignment with stakeholders and efficient use of resources, focusing on cost reduction and enhancing customer and operational experiences.

What you'll do...

The Senior Manager, Process Improvement drives the strategic development and delivery of projects aimed at improving customer/associate experience, operational efficiency, and reduce the cost to serve. This role may develop multi-year strategic roadmaps, ensuring initiatives align with financial commitments and corporate goals. The position also involves frequent updates to senior leadership on project progress and outcomes.

Collaboration and coordination with various stakeholders, including internal teams and external partners, are essential for end-to-end project delivery, including meeting project timelines, budgets, and success criteria. The role requires managing and developing a team to support change management strategies, including communication and training to ensure the adoption and sustainment of new processes or technologies.

The Senior Manager, Process Improvement recruits, onboards, and develops team members, ensuring they are equipped with the necessary tools and knowledge. This role may also work with relevant stakeholders to gain alignment on where initiatives will have cross-functional impacts, and is accountable for leading the successful execution, launch, hypercare and BAU hand-off, ensuring best practices are followed throughout.

Lastly, the role includes developing business cases for new initiatives, collaborating with finance and other departments to ensure ROI metrics are integrated into planning processes. The Senior Manager, Process Improvement champions customer experience and feedback, using insights to shape future strategies and prioritize initiatives for continuous improvement.


Leadership Expectations:

Respect the Individual:

Demonstrates and encourages respect for all; builds a high-performing team; seeks, and embraces differences in people, cultures, ideas and experiences; creates a workplace and experiences where all associates feel seen, supported and connected through culture of belonging so associates thrive and perform; drives a positive associate and customer experience for all; identifies, attracts, and retains the best team members.

Creates a discipline and focus around developing talent, through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and developmental opportunities; promotes an environment allowing everyone to bring their best selves to work; empowers associates and partners to act in the best interest of the customer and company; and regularly recognizes others’ contributions and accomplishments.

Builds strong and trusting relationships with team members and business partners; works collaboratively and cross-functionally to achieve objectives; and communicates and listens attentively, with energy and positivity to motivate, influence, and inspire commitment and action.

Acts with Integrity:

Maintains and promotes the highest standards of integrity, ethics and compliance; models the Walmart values and leads by example to foster our culture; supports Walmart’s goal of becoming a regenerative company by making a positive impact for associates, customers, and the world around us (e.g., creating a sense of belonging, eliminating waste, participating in local giving).

Follows the law, our code of conduct and company policies, and sets expectations for others to do the same; promotes an environment where associates feel comfortable sharing concerns and reinforces our culture of non-retaliation; listens to concerns raised by associates. takes action and encourages others to do the same; holds self and others accountable for achieving results in a way that is consistent with our values.

Acts as an altruistic servant leader and is consistently humble, self-aware, honest, and transparent.

Serve our Customers:

Delivers expected business results while putting the customer first and consistently applying an omni-merchant mindset and acts with an Every Day Low Cost mindset to drive value and Every Day Low Prices for customers.

Adopts a holistic perspective that considers data, analytics, customer insights, and different parts of the business when making plans and shaping the team’s strategy.

Strive for Excellence:

Consistently raises the bar and seeks to improve; demonstrates curiosity and a growth mindset; seeks feedback, asks thoughtful questions, fosters an environment that supports learning, innovation, and learning from mistakes, and intelligent risk-taking; and exhibits resilience in the face of setbacks.

Seeks and implements continuous improvements and encourages the team to leverage new digital tools and ways of working.

title: Senior Analyst, Events Operations
description:
Position Summary...

This role supports the coordination and execution of business initiatives through asset management, event planning, project support, stakeholder engagement, data analysis, and vendor coordination. The role may contribute to operational improvements, support business objectives, and help drive effective execution of activities across functional areas.

What you'll do...

This role supports the planning, coordination, and execution of operational and business activities. The role may assist with managing physical and digital assets, maintaining asset records, and ensuring assets are utilized, maintained, and stored according to established standards, requirements, and processes.

This role may gather, analyze, and interpret data to support business decisions and operational effectiveness. The role also leverages available technologies, reporting tools, and digital solutions to support transactional activities, improve data quality, identify insights, and contribute to process improvements and automation opportunities.

This role may support the planning and delivery of projects, events, and business initiatives by coordinating activities, monitoring timelines, identifying risks, tracking progress, and assisting with issue resolution. The role also contributes to event coordination, budget tracking, vendor engagement, and the delivery of materials and resources needed to achieve business objectives.

This role builds and maintains productive relationships with stakeholders, vendors, and partners through effective communication and collaboration. The role may assist in preparing communications, presentations, meeting materials, and other business deliverables, while supporting the implementation of business solutions, continuous improvement efforts, and compliance with organizational policies, standards, and ethical practices.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Event Management, Hospitality, Finance, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience considered.
  • 3–5 years of relevant experience in event operations, event budgeting, sourcing/procurement, hospitality, finance or project coordination, ideally supporting large-scale corporate events.
  • Strong experience with budget management, forecasting, financial tracking, invoice reconciliation and reporting, with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Experience supporting vendor sourcing, procurement, contract administration and supplier management, including coordination with internal partners and external vendors.
  • Strong project coordination and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, deadlines and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience supporting event operations and logistics across complex events involving multiple stakeholders, suppliers and significant attendee volumes.
  • Strong Excel and analytical skills, with experience using technology and tools to improve processes, reporting and operational efficiency.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify cost efficiencies and process improvements while maintaining event quality and supporting EDLC principles.
  • Strong communication, collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams and with external partners.
  • Proven problem-solving skills and sound judgment, with the ability to anticipate issues, identify solutions and support successful event execution.
  • Experience working within a large, complex corporate environment and supporting high-profile leadership, associate or supplier events is preferred.
  • No supervisory experience required, but the individual should be comfortable coordinating work across multiple internal teams and external partners.
  • Must be able to lift 50 pounds
  • Occasional travel across Canada & US



Preferred Qualifications:


  • Experience supporting major corporate conferences, leadership meetings, associate events or supplier summits;
  • Experience with sourcing/procurement platforms and event-management technology; and demonstrated experience supporting events ranging from hundreds to thousands of attendees.




Leadership Expectations:

Respect the Individual:

Demonstrates and encourages respect for others; drives a positive associate and customer experience for all; embraces differences in people, cultures, ideas, and experiences; supports workplaces where associated feel seen and connected through a culture of belonging, so all associates thrive and perform; contributes to an environment allowing everyone to bring their best selves to work.
Demonstrates engagement and commitment to the team, developing others through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and developmental opportunities; and recognizes others’ contributions and accomplishments.
Builds strong and trusting relationships with team members and business partners; works collaboratively to achieve objectives; communicates with impact and listens attentively to a range of audiences; and demonstrates energy and positivity for own work.

Acts with Integrity:

Maintains and promotes the highest standards of integrity, ethics and compliance; models the Walmart values and leads by example to foster our culture; supports Walmart’s goal of becoming a regenerative company by making a positive impact for associates, customers, and the world around us (e.g., creating a sense of belonging, eliminating waste, participating in local giving).
Follows the law, our code of conduct and company policies, and encourages others to do the same; supports an environment where associates feel comfortable sharing concerns; reinforces our culture of non-retaliation; listens to concerns raised by associates and takes action; acts with accountability for achieving results in a way that is consistent with our values.
Is consistently humble, self-aware, honest, and transparent.

Serve our Customers:

Delivers results while putting the customer first and applying an omni-merchant mindset and acts with an Every Day Low Cost mindset to drive value and Every Day Low Prices for customers.
Adopts a broad perspective that considers data, analytics, customer insights, and different parts of the business when making plans.

Strive for Excellence:

Consistently raises the bar and seeks to improve; demonstrates curiosity and a growth mindset; seeks feedback, asks thoughtful questions; supports innovation and intelligent risk-taking; and exhibits resilience in the face of setbacks.
Implements and supports continuous improvements and willingly embraces new digital tools and ways of working.

title: Software Developer I
description:
We’re HCSS. We’re a software company based in Sugar Land, TX providing innovative solutions that help streamline operations for construction companies. Our mission at HCSS is to help customers dramatically improve their business through our innovative, high-quality software and exceptionally helpful service while providing a great life for our employees. We’re recognized as a pioneer and leader in our market, and one of the “Best Companies to Work for in Texas” 16 years in a row.

WHO WE NEED:
Are you a Computer Science Graduate (or any similar logical discipline) who’s early in your Development career, but feels your tech skills have stagnated? At HCSS, we’ll PAY and TEACH you to grow with us as a Software Developer, building software products for the construction industry.
During your first three months, you’ll go through a rigorous training program learning .NET programming and completing assignments to demonstrate a command of languages, libraries, and other programming tools. We keep our class sizes small so you have more 1:1 attention with the instructor.

If you're a fit, the following things should sound like you:
  • You are a problem solver and have the ability to think logically and communicate clearly
  • You learn quickly and take the initiative to utilize resources outside of what is provided in order to succeed
  • Looking to grow your career further within Software Development

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Interact with a team of 3-6 developers and other stakeholders to develop features that enhance your assigned software product
  • Produce code that follows current team coding standards (syntax, naming, etc.)
  • Test your own code to ensure there are no obvious defects before committing
  • Receive critical feedback on your work openly and improve/correct your code as needed
  • Advance your knowledge of programming languages, libraries, and tools used by your team
  • Develop a working knowledge of your product(s)’ existing architecture
  • Learn and apply existing software patterns in your work
  • Assist debugging for support escalations and in teammates’ code
  • Grow your understanding of Agile development methodology by contributing to team meetings

WHY WORK WITH OUR DEVELOPMENT TEAM?
  • Build products of real value. We work as partners with our customers from the construction industry by understanding their problems and offering modern technical solutions.
  • Freedom to fail. We focus more on someone’s strengths than their current title or role. People are encouraged to offer unexpected solutions that challenge the normal way of doing things.
  • Be a mentor and coach. We see every employee as worthy of investment, and we value people who can teach and motivate the team around them.
  • Work and fun. You are more than just the code you write. We foster an atmosphere where teams frequently organize activities and get-togethers.

BENEFITS & PERKS:
Part of our mission statement is to provide a great life for our employees. We believe that happy employees make for a better company, so we take care of them. Here are a few of the perks we offer:
  • Flexibility for you to work in-office, hybrid or remote.
  • Medical and Dental Premiums.
  • On-site amenities including a covered basketball court, soccer field, 200-meter track, etc.
  • Dog-friendly campus.
  • 401K with match.
  • Tuition reimbursement.
  • And more!

title: Claims Director
description:
Claim Director will handle a senior examiner caseload that includes severity exposures with complex coverage, compensability, litigation, or account management issues.

Claim Director will be expected to

  • Have advanced diary management, file documentation, action planning, reserve and exposure analysis skills

    Demonstrate ability to use internal and external resources to make appropriate, timely decisions independently and within authority

  • Conduct or work with SIU to direct high level investigations

  • Collaborate with medical resources to manage unusual injuries and treatment needs

  • Address compliance issues and exposures

  • Calculate and present significant reserves and settlements to internal & external customers

  • Use effective settlement strategies that leverage MSA, structure and subro issues

  • Use technical expertise and business acumen to handle account management issues

  • Develop capacity to work with the WC management team on projects like new hire on-boarding, compliance training and workflows, best practice audit follow-up

  • Mentor junior staff and help identify their training needs

  • Exceptional organizational, prioritization and time management skills

  • Open communication style that fosters continuous learning and team collaboration

  • Advanced team work, collaboration and account management skills

  • Outstanding written, oral and presentation skills that are effective with a wide variety of internal and external customers.

  • Strong business acumen and understanding of the fundamental components of claims, underwriting, agency relationships, industry strategies and trends.

  • High level of accuracy with claim financials: benefits issuance, bill payment, coding, reserves and inventory management and ability to articulate the impact of claims transactions on internal and external customer’s interests.

  • Exceptional negotiation skills and resources with demonstrated ability to coach others in use of these techniques.

  • Extensive knowledge of insurance contracts, investigation techniques, legal requirements, state compliance and insurance regulations.

  • Minimum of 5 years of work comp claims handling experience.

  • College degree or equivalent business experience.

  • Ability to work independently and assimilate learning materials on many different subjects from various sources.

  • Excellent interpersonal communications, computer and negotiation skills.

  • Ability to deal with customers in a professional manner.

title: Data Engineer
description:
We are working with a leading organisation seeking a Data Engineer to join its growing data team. This is a hands‑on role focused on building, optimising and maintaining an Azure‑based data platform that supports analytics and reporting across the business.

You’ll play a key role in developing scalable data pipelines, enhancing data quality, and ensuring business users have access to reliable, high‑quality datasets. This position would suit someone who enjoys execution‑focused engineering work and wants to contribute directly to the evolution of a modern cloud data platform.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop and optimise data pipelines using Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse Analytics
  • Build and maintain robust data storage solutions within Azure Data Lake and Synapse
  • Develop high‑performance SQL transformations and data processing workflows
  • Monitor platform performance and continuously improve reliability, scalability and efficiency
  • Ensure data quality, integrity and consistency across the data landscape
  • Work closely with analysts and business stakeholders to deliver trusted datasets for reporting and analytics
  • Support data governance, security and compliance initiatives
  • Identify opportunities to improve existing processes, data flows and platform capabilities

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in Data Engineering, ideally within a Microsoft Azure environment
  • Strong hands‑on SQL development and optimisation skills
  • Experience building and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines
  • Proven expertise with Azure Synapse Analytics and Azure Data Factory
  • Experience working with Azure Data Lake or similar cloud‑based storage solutions
  • Good understanding of data modelling, schema design and database concepts
  • Experience handling large‑scale datasets and developing scalable data solutions
  • Strong analytical mindset with a practical, delivery‑focused approach
  • Able to challenge existing solutions and contribute ideas for continuous improvement
  • Excellent stakeholder communication skills and the ability to work with both technical and non‑technical teams
  • Fluent English communication skills
  • Dutch language skills are essential

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Python for data processing and automation
  • Exposure to data governance and data quality frameworks
  • Familiarity with cloud security and compliance best practices
  • Experience operating within enterprise‑scale data environment

What’s on Offer

  • Opportunity to work on a modern Azure data platform
  • Exposure to large‑scale data and analytics initiatives
  • Collaborative and highly skilled data team
  • Long‑term career development and progression opportunities
  • Flexible working environment with a hybrid working model

title: Engagement Lead
description:
We are looking for an experienced Engagement Lead to join our Gas & Power ETRM Consulting Practice, replacing a senior leader within the team and taking ownership of strategic client engagements across trading and energy transformation initiatives.
This role is ideal for a professional who combines deep gas and power trading domain expertise with strong consulting, delivery, and stakeholder management capabilities. The successful candidate will be comfortable working across front office, risk, operations, and IT teams, helping clients shape and deliver complex trading and ETRM programmes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead client engagements across gas and power trading transformation programmes.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to trading, risk, and technology stakeholders.
  • Drive the delivery of ETRM-related projects, including system implementation, optimisation, migration, and process transformation.
  • Translate trading business requirements into scalable functional and technical solutions.
  • Structure, analyse, and interpret complex trading datasets across front-to-back trading environments.
  • Manage senior client relationships and support business development activities.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams, including business analysts, architects, developers, and vendor teams.
  • Contribute to practice growth, delivery standards, and industry thought leadership.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Strong experience within gas and power trading environments.
  • Deep understanding of physical and/or financial energy trading workflows, including trade lifecycle, scheduling and nominations, risk and P&L, settlements, and market operations.
  • Proven consulting or programme delivery experience in ETRM/CTRM environments.
  • Strong analytical and data-structuring capabilities within trading IT ecosystems.
  • Ability to engage effectively with both business and technical stakeholders.
  • Experience leading client-facing engagements and managing delivery streams.

Preferred Skills & Qualifications﻿
  • 7+ years of experience with one or more major ETRM platforms, such as Endur/Openlink, Allegro, Aspect, TriplePoint, Orchestrade, Beacon, Molecule, SAP Commodity Management, or other relevant energy trading platforms.
  • Experience in data architecture and data modelling within trading environments.
  • Exposure to cloud technologies and modern data platforms.
  • Understanding of integration architecture and APIs.
  • Knowledge of regulatory reporting and market compliance.
  • Experience with Agile delivery methodologies within trading organisations.

R-2659896

title: (CAN) Pharmacy Assistant
description:
Position Summary...

The Pharmacy Assistant assists the Pharmacist in the technical aspects of prescription filling and administrative duties in order to increase the Pharmacist's opportunity to provide patient care. The Pharmacy Assistant is expected to participate in all aspects of Pharmacy Operations required of a team player. They are a key member in the delivery of superior customer service.

What you'll do...

1. Receiving prescriptions from patients, following provincial legal/regulatory conditions and assessing the prescription for completeness i.e. Name; Address; DOB; Allergies; 3rd Party Information; Any Special Requests; Prescriber; Generic/Brand; Prioritizing Prescriptions with 21st Century Guidelines.
2. Performing Computer Functions as directed by the Pharmacist i.e. Data Entry; Price Check; Patient Information Entry/Update; Competent interpretation and processing of written prescriptions including Latin abbreviations, drug name recognition, dosage calculations; Refills; Report Generation; Patient Profile checks.
3. Filling prescriptions (always under the Pharmacist’s supervision), selecting appropriate products, performing the accuracy program, including 7 point, Visual and DIN checks, selecting and counting/ measuring & preparing appropriate products, labeling and organizing for pharmacist checking, gaining necessary approvals for verbal refills where authorized, employing 'STOP' forms if applicable and facilitating all aspects of Cognitive Services.
4. Maintaining Inventory Control, assisting Pharmacist in maintaining appropriate stock levels of drugs and supplies, checking for and pulling expired medications at least monthly, cleaning up Will Call Bin of 'stale' prescriptions on a regular basis, writing up returns, ordering of drugs and supplies, using preferred wholesaler for Pharmacy purchases as much as possible i.e. Kohl and Frisch, operating of the Telxon gun, checking off, pricing and putting away pharmacy orders, zoning the pharmacy shelves, 'X- ing' bottles when opened and interchangeable drug knowledge and appropriate maintenance/selection of key brands/preferred generics.
5. General Housekeeping, stocking Prescription filling supplies (Vials, labels, bags), keeping the dispensary clean, organized and neat, maintaining clean/safe work environment as part of the team approach (i.e. dishes, garbage) and maintaining & cleaning packaging & dispensing equipment, computer, fax machine, etc.
6. Clerical Organization, filing prescriptions, invoices, reports, correspondence and memos and completing any administrative support functions assigned (i.e. journals, accounts receivable, Aged Trial Balance).
7. Assisting with OTC Operations and ordering, stocking, cashier duties as assigned by OTC Manager and/or Pharmacist.

The pay range for this position is $17.60 - $23.10/hr. Rate of pay will be determined based on relevant experience.
